questions: Should the function handle lists containing non-numeric elements (e.g., strings, tuples) and sort them appropriately?
If the lists contain duplicate common elements, should the output include each unique element only once, as implied by 'unique'?
Is the sorting order always ascending, even for mixed types or negative numbers?
Should the function preserve the original order of elements before sorting, or is any order acceptable before applying sorted?
What should happen if the input lists are not lists (e.g., tuples, generators)?
Are there any constraints on list size or performance expectations (e.g., time complexity)?
Should the function modify the input lists in any way (e.g., sorting them in-place)?
How should the function handle nested lists or mutable elements where equality might be deep vs. shallow?
